claims.text: A tunable NiAl interlayer can enable a controlled transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep in HEA multilayers.
Introducing NiAl between HEA layers establishes highly coherent interfaces.
NiAl has an intermediate atomic diffusivity relevant to controlling creep in HEA multilayers.
The proposed starting material is a multilayer coating composed of HEA layers with designed coherent interfaces.
The NiAl interlayer thickness and composition can be adjusted between HEA layers.
Diffusion creep and dislocation creep are both active under the proposed elevated-temperature creep conditions.
Highly coherent interfaces form between the NiAl interlayer and adjacent HEA layers.
NiAl can form coherent interfaces with many FCC HEA matrices.
The coherent NiAl interfaces and intermediate diffusivity modulate the balance between atomic diffusion and dislocation mobility.
The NiAl interlayer creates a transitional region in which the dominant creep mechanism changes gradually.
Lower stresses or temperatures favor diffusion-mediated creep.
Higher stresses or temperatures favor dislocation-mediated creep.
The creep-mechanism transition will occur under more controlled and intermediate conditions with a NiAl interlayer than without one.
In HEA multilayers without NiAl, the transition between creep mechanisms is less defined and is not intentionally regulated.
The proposed effect depends on maintaining interface coherency and precise control of the interlayer.
Excessive NiAl thickness or compositional deviations may degrade interface coherency and limit the creep-transition effect.
The exact stress and temperature thresholds for the creep-mechanism switch are unknown.
TEM and XRD can be used to assess interface coherency in the proposed samples.
